replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Yep, during especially cold winters in the 1920s, parts of the Detroit River could freeze thick enough for people to cross on the ice. I didn’t mean the entire river froze solid every winter, but rum-runners did use the frozen sections when conditions allowed.
